name: action-confirmation
purpose: A user-authorized action in a conversation (Cloudscape user-authorized actions, AI Elements Confirmation): the agent proposes something with consequences — call a tool, run a command, deploy, delete — and the reader approves or denies it before anything runs. The card states the action as a question (``Allow `npm test`?``), says what will happen, shows exactly what will run in its body (a `CodeBlock` with the command, `KeyValuePairs` with parameters), and offers Deny and Approve. Once decided, the buttons give way to the outcome in text (`Approved`, `Denied`, `Request expired`) so the decision stays in the thread. Irreversible actions (`kind="danger"`) turn Approve destructive and can require typing a phrase first. It is a card in the conversation, not a dialog: it does not trap focus and does not take initial focus; `focus()` moves focus to its heading when the owner wants to bring the reader to it.
useWhen: One-time authorization of a consequential action proposed by an agent: a production deployment, a purge, a command.
avoidWhen: Tools already trusted for the session → record the call with `tool-call`, do not ask again.
A destructive action the reader started themselves in the UI → `confirm-dialog`.
A form → this card only approves or denies.
related: tool-call` — the record of the call after it is approved (or `denied`).
confirm-dialog` — confirmation of the reader's own destructive action.
code-block`, `key-value-pairs` — what will run, in the body.
chat-message` — the assistant acknowledges the decision in the next message.
bestPractices: Title is a question naming the action and target; put tool and command names in backticks (code).
Match the approve label to the title verb (`Deploy`, `Delete`) when it is not a generic tool call.
Never pre-focus or pre-select Approve for a risky action.
Do not leave a request pending forever: expire it (`state="expired"`) and have the assistant say nothing ran.
After Deny, the assistant acknowledges in the conversation ("Skipping that step.").

props.name: title
props.doc: The question, naming the action: ``Allow `npm test`?``, `Approve deployment to production?`. Backticks render as code.

props.name: description
props.doc: One or two sentences on what will happen and to what; backticks render as code.

props.name: state
props.doc: pending` asks; `approved`, `denied` and `expired` replace the buttons with the outcome in text.

props.name: kind
props.doc: danger` for an action that cannot be undone: the approve button turns destructive.

props.name: confirmationPhrase
props.doc: A word the reader must type before Approve enables, for irreversible actions (the resource name). Empty asks for no typing.

props.name: approveLabel
props.doc: Text of the approve button, the verb of the title (`Deploy`, `Delete`). Empty uses the locale catalog (`Approve`).

props.name: denyLabel
props.doc: Text of the deny button. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Deny`).

props.name: loading
props.doc: A decision is being sent; both buttons are inert and Approve shows its loading state.

slots.name: default
slots.notes: What exactly will run: a `CodeBlock`, or `KeyValuePairs` with parameters.
